newsitem.title: USA: USDA panel votes to expand crop insurance programs.
newsitem.headline: USDA panel votes to expand crop insurance programs.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department's crop insurance board voted to expand crop revenue coverage (CRC) to cover cotton, spring wheat and grain sorghum, said Ken Ackerman, head of USDA's Risk Management Agency.
Currently, the CRC covers corn, soybeans and winter wheat.
Ackerman said in an interview with USDA Radio that the panel also voted to offer a new product called "revenue assurance" on corn and soybeans in Iowa.
He also said USDA will expand the income protection program to the new crops of grain sorghum and soybeans.
The new program and the program expansions will be available in the Spring.
